seed: Objects of type `block` under action ACTION4 with touching neighbours [arm] show mixed outcomes: no_change x19, x x10. Find the condition in the before state that decides the outcome. Start from this kind of condition: a global object such as a counter, HUD element or legend, read as state. Verify it against every transition before you keep it.

synth.notes:
Ring (player)+beam (arm) move y by 6 on A1/A2, carrying on-beam blocks and pushing hit blocks; whole move cancels if a block would leave the colour-4 field.
A4/A3 extend/retract beam by 6; any block at x==tip-5 on beam rows hooks all fully-on-beam blocks to follow the tip; unhooked extend pushes the swept strip; blocked chain -> beam moves alone.
Block A4 [arm] no_change vs x is decided by this hook/push/field geometry, not by a global counter (hypothesis refuted).
Tags: hooked next alone -> collected, collected off beam reverts; legend swatch centre 2x2 = 0 while collected. Clicks are no-ops.
HUD bar row 53: 3s=(n-1)//3, n = non-click actions, kept in a memo keyed by returned frames (hidden phase; fallback 3*bars+1 or 0).
